newsitem.title: USA: GE earnings up 11 percent; sees record results for year.
newsitem.headline: GE earnings up 11 percent; sees record results for year.

text.p: General Electric Co. Thursday reported an 11 percent gain in first-quarter earnings to a new high and said it was in a position to deliver a record results for the year.

The company, whose interests range from aircraft engines to the NBC television network, said it earned $1.67 billion, or $1.02 a share, on revenues of $20.15 billion. That compared with year-earlier profits of $1.51 billion, or 91 cents a share, on revenues of $17.09 billion.
GE said 10 of its twelve businesses reported higher operating profit for the first quarter, with six, led by GE Capital Services, Power Systems and Aircraft Engines, achieving double-digit increases.
GE Capital Services' earnings were $754 million, 16 percent higher than last year's $650 million, benefiting from the globalization and diversity of its businesses.
The results were led by strong double-digit increases in Specialised Financing, Speciality Insurance and Equipment Management activities, the Fairfield, Conn., conglomerate said.
"These strong first-quarter results position GE to deliver another year of record performance in 1997," said Chairman John Welch.
"During the quarter, GE's expansion into services accelerated," he said.
GE said NBC won its ninth consecutive ratings sweep and moved its MSNBC operations into a new state-of-the-art studio during the quarter.
GE Capital continued its insurance growth with the acquisition of Coregis, Xerox's property and casualty insurance business.
GE Information Services expanded its Internet activities with a joint venture with Thomas Publishing and a new venture with Netscape.
GE's stock was off 50 cents at $101.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in early trading.
